description: Graphite with 90k CMC at total 16 g/L: the compact phenomenological net potential screens the complete legacy potential including the RE2 tail. The 450 pN reference attraction gains conservative coordination saturation; the explicit pair repulsion remains 20 pN, while coordination adds a geometry-dependent entry cost. The bare contact gap stays 2 nm.

numerics._absolute_tolerance_reference: The net potential can have an orientation-dependent barrier of about 0.3 pN. These absolute residual tolerances resolve forces below that scale; relative tolerance and all iteration/substep limits are unchanged. This change is specific to the 16 g/L case.

cmc._concentration_units: Both concentrations are g CMC per litre of aqueous phase. Adsorbed and free inputs are independent; excess adsorbed input is capped, never transferred to free CMC.
cmc._saturation_reference: Gwag et al., ACS Nano, DOI 10.1021/acsnano.6c10201: apparent adsorption 0.37 +/- 0.09 wt% per particle mass (Gr+CB). Approximate reference conversion for this graphite-water model (neglecting the small CMC share of the paper's total solids): 0.0037 * 997 g/L * 0.44 / 0.56 = 2.8984214285714285 g/L aqueous phase. This is a converted model benchmark, not a directly reported 2.9 g/L measurement. Reassess this explicit reference if solids loading or material changes.
cmc._adhesion_model: Legacy branch: theta=min(adsorbed_g_L/adsorbed_saturation_g_L,1); q=(1-(1-sqrt(q_sat))*theta)^2; W_eff=W_bg+q*(W_bare-W_bg). interaction.adhesion_work_J_m2 remains the bare graphite reference. The net-potential blend below acts on the complete legacy potential, not just this excess adhesion.
cmc._q_sat_reference: 0.33 is the agreed starting benchmark for saturated excess-adhesion retention, not a measured CMC constant.
cmc._free_cmc_units: free_g_L is already g CMC per litre of aqueous phase: 1 g/L = 1 kg/m3. It is not total CMC; do not subtract adsorbed CMC again or apply a solids-volume factor. Free CMC is never capped or increased by the adsorbed-input clamp.
cmc._free_repulsion_model: Legacy branch: P=strength*osmotic_coefficient*DS/M0*R*T*free_g_L; Phi_outer=pi*lambda_D*P*ell^2*exp(-(H-h0)/ell). Ws=inner_work_per_g_L_J_m2*free_g_L; Phi_inner=pi*lambda_D*Ws*delta/p*(1-(H-h0)/delta)^p for H-h0<delta, zero otherwise. Both differentiate the full potential including curvature. enabled gates both repulsions; strength scales only the outer term. These parameters remain available when the net model is disabled or partially blended.
cmc._free_repulsion_reference: Trial constitutive parameters, not measured graphite-CMC force constants. Disabling net_potential restores the outer-plus-inner legacy model; additionally setting inner_work_per_g_L_J_m2=0 restores its outer-only form. Medium viscosity and friction remain explicit independent inputs.
cmc._net_potential_model: Phenomenological total-potential screening: blend=clamp((free_g_L-start_free_g_L)/(full_free_g_L-start_free_g_L),0,1); U=(1-blend)*U_legacy(free_g_L)+blend*U_net. The legacy branch uses the same current free concentration, not a frozen 4 g/L potential. At full blend the legacy adsorption, outer/inner repulsion and entire RE2 tail are replaced. U_net is zero at and beyond h0+attraction_range_m+repulsion_range_m=9 nm. Geometry scales with local Derjaguin length divided by reference a*a/c, derived from the configured semiaxes (13.6125 micrometres here). Force parameters specify the reference geometry, not every orientation.
cmc._net_potential_reference: Unmeasured starting constitutive parameters. Activation starts at the saturated-adsorption 4 g/L benchmark and reaches full strength at 16 g/L. The shipped 4 g/L case and pure graphite retain their legacy laws. This is an explicit hypothesis for concentration-dependent total interactions, not a claim of established molecular screening.
cmc._coordination_model: Only net attraction is modified: E_A=sum_ij g(z_i-q_ij)*g(z_j-q_ij)*A_ij, z_i=sum_j q_ij. The smooth neighbor weight q falls from 1 at h0 to 0 at h0+attraction_range_m using 1-10t^3+15t^4-6t^5. Each endpoint factor g is 1 up to one other neighbor and decreases by the same quintic to 0.1 at two other neighbors; the pair factor is their product (minimum 0.01). Forces and torques differentiate the full energy, including coordination derivatives. The explicit pair repulsion is unchanged; coordination adds a geometry-dependent entry cost. Disabling coordination restores the pair-additive net potential at the configured force amplitude.
cmc._initialization: The common 10 nm initial clearance exceeds the active net potential's 9 nm support. This is only a geometric initial-placement condition; rough_contact.roughness_gap_m remains 2 nm and no aging or preshear is performed by initialization.
